evidence: The pooled ring removal bins |Q| from 1.5 to 10.5 Å⁻¹ whatever the volume holds (RingParams.q_min, q_max: src/nebula3d/_ringplane.py:59-60), and its detector, _detect_rings (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/radial_background.py:1321), took the noise its candidates must rise pooled_min_snr = 6 times (_ringplane.py:101), 1.4826·median(|diff(g − rough)|)/√2, over every bin (radial_background.py:1364). The bins no plane samples (NaN in the pooled profile) are filled by _fill_nan_1d, edge-extended, so flat past the last measured bin (:1309-1318, :1348), the sparse ones interpolated across (:1352-1357), and SNIP (:1358) leaves a flat run as it is: there g − rough is exactly 0. On a volume whose counts end well inside 10.5 Å⁻¹, once about half the differences were 0 the noise was 0, the 6σ floor went, and every local maximum became a candidate. The candidates above the noise are kept out of the judged shells' flanks (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/pooled_rings.py:560-566; src/nebula3d/preprocessing/ring_isotropy.py:309-311), so a real ring's isotropy test drew its line through two or three flank bins (a signal-to-noise of about 1e14 to 1e16) and skipped its curve check, which needs four (ring_isotropy.py:454). Measured on 39b0835 (synthetic volumes only): of the validation's dev cases, whose box reaches 6.44 Å⁻¹ at its faces and 11.16 Å⁻¹ at its corners, only dev-coverage ends inside the range (counts cut at 4.511 Å⁻¹, no ring). At n=161, 151 of its 224 bins are empty, the noise is 0 (0.0074 over the measured bins), 24 candidates, 18 judged and rejected as the crystal's own, none subtracted. At n=81, 77 of 112 bins are empty and its 10 candidates are all listed in the coarse-grid notice (G1), whose remedy, pooled_confirm_rings=False, subtracted all ten as rings (1.70 to 3.96 Å⁻¹, 9.4 % of |I|). The dev crystal at n=161 with no counts past 4 Å⁻¹ and rings planted at 2.2 and 3.3 Å⁻¹: candidates at 2.00 and 2.41 Å⁻¹ left the 2.2 ring a signal-to-noise of 9.9e15 and no curve check. Against where its counts end, the dev crystal's noise at n=161 is 0 from 4 to 5.5 Å⁻¹, 0.04 of the measured noise at 6 to 6.5, 0.28 at 7, 0.45 at 7.5, 0.60 at 8, 0.73 at 9 and 0.90 at 10.
proposed_fix: (b) The noise from the measured bins only: _measured_noise takes the MAD of the residual's bin-to-bin differences, /√2, over the pairs of adjacent bins that are both measured (finite in the pooled profile, and not sparse: sampled by a tenth of the median number of planes or more), and is inf with no such pair, so nothing then passes the floor. With every bin measured it is the estimate over all the bins, as before. Weighed and left out: (c), a ring judged only on two flank bins a side or more, else not judged, with a retry that keeps out the confirmed rings alone, which never fired with (b) in place; docs/pipeline.md keeps it as an option. IsotropyConfig.min_cells is not changed (the open question in the note).

note: Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19, as a freeze blocker. Against main (39b0835): every dev case's ring-removed volume at n=81 and n=161 is bit-identical (16 of 16, dev-coverage's too: with pooled_confirm_rings on, the flood was rejected or left unconfirmed, never subtracted), and so is the synthetic demo volume's at 161³ and 61³ (at 161³ the old noise estimate is 1.06 times the new one). The new tests fail on main (5 of the 7; the other two pin _measured_noise itself). Arm A on dev re-run: 32 of 32 entries identical, 5 of 8 cases pass, as recorded; 21 of its 24 run logs unchanged, dev-coverage's three differing in the ring line alone (no_confirmed_rings with 18 shells not confirmed, now no_rings with none). On volumes constructed with their counts cut short, the candidates fall from 14–37 to 0–6, every false shell the flood made is gone, and strong rings are judged on two flank bins a side (signal-to-noise 37 to 64, curve 0.92 to 1.05); weak rings under the restored 6σ floor go undetected, as on full coverage. Left: (c) is an option not taken (docs/pipeline.md). Outside this finding, a known limit: a weak ring (amplitude 0.05 beside one of 0.5) is subtracted at 1.2 to 2.4 times its amplitude in every geometry tried, full coverage included. Open for the user: between a box's face and its corner a shell is measured in some directions only, and the isotropy test judges it on 16 to 32 of its 128 direction cells (IsotropyConfig.min_cells is 16); on a synthetic cubic crystal, shells of the crystal's own pass there as rings whatever the noise (4.41 Å⁻¹ on a ±3 Å⁻¹ box; 5.01, 5.49, 7.29 and 9.01 Å⁻¹ on others). min_cells = 64, half the sphere, with (b) removes all of them, keeps every planted ring and leaves the dev cases identical, but whether a ring may be confirmed from part of the sphere, and from how much of it, is the user's rule, so min_cells is unchanged.
